citation_note: Primary CCL3/CCR1 neutrophil-migration and CCR1 Gi-coupling studies
evidence_summary: CCL3/MIP-1alpha receptor-specific evidence supports CCR1-dependent neutrophil migration and sequential TNF-alpha/LTB4 release. A separate primary CCR1 reconstitution study supports pertussis-toxin-sensitive Gi-family coupling and PLC signaling. Together these provide a bounded CCL3-CCR1-Gi-to-cellular-output route without assigning a terminal TF or target gene.
limitations: The ligand-specific migration studies and the CCR1 Gi-coupling study are composite evidence from different systems; preserve the receptor, species, pertussis-toxin and neutrophil-model boundaries. Do not infer a single Gi isoform, SCI response or transcriptional endpoint.

citation_note: Primary CCL3/CCR5 neutrophil-migration and CCR5 GNAZ-coupling studies
evidence_summary: CCL3/MIP-1alpha receptor-specific evidence supports CCR5-associated signaling and neutrophil migration involving ERK1/2 and p38. A separate primary CCR5 subtype-coupling profile supports GNAZ activation in a human heterologous system. These composite records support a bounded CCL3-CCR5-GNAZ-to-cellular-output route without assigning a terminal TF or target gene.
limitations: The CCL3 functional studies and the GNAZ coupling profile use different ligands and systems; preserve the MIP-1alpha stimulation context of the coupling assay and do not treat GNAZ as the exclusive CCR5 transducer. No SCI or transcriptional endpoint is inferred.

evidence_summary: Primary CCL5/RANTES studies support receptor-specific CCR5 binding and activation, including an active CCR5-Gi complex.
